text:
rachel: quick thought dump: rather than separate prefetch-owner vs live-owner RPC, what if we piggyback owner tokens onto existing health/lease heartbeats? reduces extra RPCs and keeps connection affinity.

dong: interesting. piggybacking saves ops, but does it increase coupling between liveness and ownership? what about nodes that don't talk frequently?

rachel: plan: two headers on worker->worker calls: X-Owner-Token (opt) and X-Epoch (opt). control-plane issues canonical tokens, workers renew via lease-heartbeat every 700ms for hot prefixes. if a worker hasn't talked in >2s we consider it stale.

maya: curious about zero-copy buffers. earlier sharing relied on refcounts across processes. does token piggyback change lifecycle for shared buf refs?

rachel: yes, we make a distinction: ownership token authorizes mutating handoffs and pin semantics, but underlying buffer memory is reference-counted and can be aliased across tenants. tokens do not gate memory frees directly; instead, release triggers an invalidation marker + refcount decrement. frees only happen when refs==0 and no valid owner epoch.

omar: so we might have a window where owner released but memory still referenced by stale readers. risk of reading freed memory reduced by refcount, ok. but what about dangling metadata like shard pointers?

rachel: metadata includes a small GUID and epoch in headers. any reader validates GUID+epoch against local registry; mismatch => read returns MISS and optionally fetches fresh. this keeps stale pointers from being followed.

sanjay: migration question: we'll need to repopulate registry GUIDs for prefixes. propose a sweep that assigns GUIDs and bumps epoch atomically in control-plane with throttling. target low-traffic prefixes first.

maya: metric needs: owner_header_hit_ratio, lease_renew_rate, orphaned_ref_count_gauge, aliasing_conflicts_total, slow_proxy_fallback_total. also add per-tenant memory_shared_bytes so we can detect cross-tenant alias spikes.

dong: fallback behavior in mixed-version clusters? older nodes will ignore owner headers. how to avoid double-ownership during rollout?

rachel: fallback: if a worker sees no owner header, it treats prefix as legacy and uses slow serial handoff (proxy) that obtains a ephemeral token via control-plane CAS. proxy has bounded concurrency and circuit-breaks. we'll surface slow_proxy_fallback_total.

omar: can the proxy be distributed? a small pool per region to avoid single hot spot. also add token pre-warm for hot tenants.

rachel: yes region-local proxy pools. tokens can be pre-warmed when traffic exceeds threshold T_hot (e.g., 100 RPS per prefix in 1m).

sanjay: operational playbook: how to detect owner leaks? steps: 1) query owner_registry for prefix, 2) check last_renew_ts, 3) gather refcount snapshot, 4) if last_renew > reclaim_threshold, issue admin reclaim CAS and watch orphaned_ref_count. add safety: force reclaim only if orphaned_ref_count==0 or after grace window.

maya: +1. add a debug endpoint that simulates reclaim without applying to let us dry-run.

dong: eviction policy change? currently LRU-ish. tokens enable eviction to prefer demote over immediate free for prefixes with recent owner activity. propose eviction grace 500ms-2s depending on tier.

rachel: exact policy: if owner_epoch matches and last_renew < grace_window => demote to cold tier (keep KV fragments but remove hot pins). if owner is stale => tombstone + invalidate subscribers. buffer free only after refcount hits zero or tombstone TTL expires (default 30s).

omar: tests to catch races: 1) concurrent release+read where read arrives during tombstone TTL; 2) double-claim where two nodes get acquire at same ms; 3) mixed-version proxy fallback under load. we should add fuzz tests that vary network delays and notebook load.

sanjay: rollout: opt-in flag per pool, then canary in non-prod region for 24h; then turn on reads by default in more regions; then enable mutating handoffs with long canary and proxy-limited concurrency.

rachel: deploy-bot: note that the canary bucket in staging has capacity for one rollout this weekend. book via #release-war-room.

deploy-bot: Canary window available: Sat 02:00-06:00 UTC. Use tag "owner-token-canary-1" when scheduling.

omar: last ask: can we make token id compact and cache-friendly? maybe 64-bit monotonic plus 16-bit shard id. avoids big UUID allocations in hot loops.

rachel: agreed, token format: {shard:16, epoch:48, seq:64} encoded in 16 bytes hex. small and fast to compare.

maya: great. @rachel can you open the RFC follow-up with the piggyback diagram, token format, test matrix, metric list, and rollout checklist? I'll queue infra for proxy pool sizes.

rachel: will do. linking when ready. thanks everyone.
